newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends steady to firmer in choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends steady to firmer in choppy trade.

text.p: NWE gasoline was firm to a tad stronger on Tuesday in a choppy day dictated largely by volatile price action on the NYMEX energy complex, traders said.
Eurograde barges traded at $195.50 and $195 a tonne fob ARA pre-May 6 delivery in the morning, but later similar parcels traded at $192 and $193. Regular barges traded at $187 fob ARA.
May swaps traded in a $196/$199.50 band throughout the day and were talked at $197/$198 in later trade.
Traders attributed the price fluctuations to the changeable fortunes of crude and gasoline futures as the day progressed.
IPE Brent was 23 cents off at $18.11 a barrel at 1735 GMT, having traded as high as $18.64. NYMEX gasoline was trading 1.05 cents off at 61.75 cents a gallon.
On the cargo front, a small 10,000-tonne premium unleaded cargo traded at $197 fob Wilhelmshaven, Germany.
There was talk that two cargoes traded on Monday with trans-Atlantic destinations but this was not confirmed.
Shipbrokers reported, however, that Statoil had chartered a 33,000 tonne clean vessel bound for either the U.S. Gulf or Atlantic Coast loading May 28.
Two Scandinavian players were also reported to be offering cargoes into northern Germany but had not received "satisfactory" bids.
A number of refiners were taking a relaxed approach to gasoline sales in the expectation that prices can only get better in the medium term, traders said.
"With the contango in place, sellers are fairly relaxed they're quite prepared to put material into storage if they can't get the number they want," one trader said.
